The video showcases the creation and viewing of celestial bodies through telescopes. It starts with a man wearing a white lab coat standing indoors, gesturing with his hands as he talks to the camera. The scene then cuts to close-ups of two camera lenses, followed by the same man setting up a silver "Celestron Explorer DX" telescope. We see what appears to be Jupiter through a blurry lens, before the video shows a different telescope, and cuts to views of deep space and nebulae. A man wearing a dark shirt, a baseball cap that reads "Robert Oatley", and glasses looks at a can. The next scenes include the man driving a car with the same baseball cap. A pair of sneakers kick a can across a patio. A telescope view of Mars is shown. A man throws a hat at the camera. Lastly, an aerial view reveals a satellite dish surrounded by solar panels. Then, the word "STAR STUFF" and "WITH DYLAN O'DONNELL" appear on the screen. The video ends with the man wearing a white lab coat inside a tent-like structure, explaining that there is construction next door while holding his hand up and gesturing with his fingers spread.

The video segment features a man’s hand touching a Celestron telescope in a dimly lit room with red lights. The telescope is silver and black, with an off-axis guider and guide camera attached. The man demonstrates how the image train goes straight into the off-axis guider, explaining how the camera chip sits in landscape mode, with the prism positioned so it doesn’t get in the way. He then points to a filter drawer that is currently blank. A graphic illustration shows the image circle, camera chip, and off-axis guide prism of the camera attached to the telescope. The brand name "CELESTRON" is visible in the lower left corner in white text with the Celestron logo, an orange stylized sun.

The video segment starts with a close-up shot of a camera attached to a black telescope, with a hand touching the camera. The camera is a QHYCCD camera, which is also written in English at the bottom of the frame, and is described as a fantastic 16-bit APC-sized camera. The scene transitions to show the Sky-Watcher EQ8-Rh PRO mount, described as a rock solid mount, followed by an image of the formula used in PixInsight for weighting, a text overlaid on top of the mount. Then the focus shifts towards the interior of the dome, noting "SOME MINOR LEAKS PERSIST..." The inside of the dome is lined with lights, with wiring and boxes attached to its ceiling. An image of the moon then fills the screen. The video then switches to show shelves and a desk filled with astronomical equipment. The scene ends with a man dressed in a white lab coat sitting in a blue chair in a living room.
